notes: Source is the diocese's own "Calendar of Intersessions" (its title on the source spreadsheet's own sheet, "Diocesan Intersessions Calendar"; "Intersessions" is the spreadsheet's own spelling throughout, not corrected to "Intercessions"), a genuinely DAILY cycle (every calendar day, not weekly) fetched directly as an .xlsx from https://diopa.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/Calendar-of-Intersessions-2025-2026.xlsx and read with openpyxl. Its real content runs continuously from Sunday, November 30, 2025 (1st Sunday of Advent) through Saturday, November 28, 2026 -- confirmed by walking every dated row in order and finding the dates strictly ascending and gap-free across that whole span (364 consecutive calendar days).

Per this schema's 'one file per diocese per year' rule and this corpus's existing disclose-and-exclude precedent for a source that starts a few weeks into Advent of the prior year (episcopal-atlanta-2026.json, episcopal-north-carolina-2026.json), this file holds only the 332 entries that fall in calendar 2026 (January 1 - November 28, 2026). The 32 entries in late 2025 (Sunday, November 30, 2025 through Wednesday, December 31, 2025 -- the full Advent season into the days following Christmas) are EXCLUDED here, not fabricated into a second file, and are listed in full for the record: Nov 30 'The Archbishop of Canturbury - Elect'; Dec 1 Diocese of Alabama; Dec 2 Diocese of Alaska; Dec 3 The Standing Committee; Dec 4 St. Peters in the Great Valley, Malvern; Dec 5 Church of St. Asaph, Bala Cynwyd; Dec 6 St. George - St. Barnabas, Philadelphia; Dec 7 The Episcopal/Anglican Provice of Alexandria; Dec 8 Diocese of Albany; Dec 9 Diocese of Arizona; Dec 10 The Diocesan Commission on Ministry; Dec 11 St. Peter's, Glenside; Dec 12 St. Andrew's, West Vincent; Dec 13 St. John's, Lower Merion; Dec 14 The Anglican Church in Aotearoa, New Zealand and Polynesia; Dec 15 Diocese of Arkansas; Dec 16 Diocese of Atlanta; Dec 17 The Church Foundation; Dec 18 Incarnation Holy Sacrament, Drexel Hill; Dec 19 St. Andrew's, Yardley; Dec 20 Church of the Redeemer, Andalusia; Dec 21 The Church of Bangladesh; Dec 22 Diocese of Bethlehem; Dec 23 Diocese of California; Dec 24 Clare Project; Dec 25 St. Michael's, Yeadon; Dec 26 Gloria Dei, Philadelphia; Dec 27 St. Paul's, Levittown; Dec 28 Igreja Episcopal Anglican do Brazil; Dec 29 Diocese of Central Ecuador; Dec 30 Diocese of Central Florida; Dec 31 Addiction Recovery Advocates Network.

PER THE ROSTER'S OWN EXPLICIT WARNING: the source workbook's rows do not stop at November 28, 2026 -- after that date the sheet repeats an old prior-year Advent template (row 701 onward), whose dates are internally inconsistent and stale (e.g. a row labeled '1st Sunday of Advent' printed against November 30, 2025 again, immediately followed by weekday rows dated in DECEMBER 2024; a '3rd Sunday of Advent' row dated 2021-12-14; a 'Thursday' row dated 2024-01-02 sitting between two 2025-dated rows). These trailing ~70 rows were identified as stale leftover template content, confirmed by the out-of-order/impossible dates, and excluded entirely -- not transcribed as 2026 (or any other) content.

This source is a genuinely DAILY cycle: every date (Sun-Sat) names exactly one subject (never more than one 'main' subject on a single date across the whole file, verified programmatically). Sunday's own subject is usually (not always) the wider Anglican Communion's weekly companion province/primate (row pattern: the liturgical-Sunday header row carries only the label+date, and an immediately following row headed 'Anglican Communion' carries the actual province/primate content for that date) -- both rows are folded into that one Sunday date's single entry per this schema's blank-date-cell grouping rule. On a handful of Sundays late in the source (Nov 8, Nov 15, and Nov 22, 2026) this Anglican-Communion sub-row is absent and the Sunday's own subject is printed directly on the header row instead (a diocesan-wide item on Nov 8/15, and a same-page continuation of the weekday 'Diocese of X' rotation on Nov 22) -- transcribed the same way regardless of which row shape carried the content.

Monday and Tuesday of nearly every week name a companion TEC diocese by name (e.g. 'Diocese of Alabama') paired with its bishop in the adjoining column -- this is the source's own nationwide diocese-by-diocese prayer rotation running roughly alphabetically across the whole year (distinct from the Sunday Anglican-Communion companion-province rotation). Both this diocese-rotation content and the Anglican-Communion content are recorded as `category` subjects (never `diocese`/`province`, which this schema reserves for scope-'communion' files only; this file's scope is 'diocese'), with the bishop/primate name from the adjoining column recorded in that subject's own `note` field, per this corpus's existing episcopal-delaware-2026.json precedent for a clergy/bishop line with no dedicated schema field of its own. By late November the alphabetical diocese list runs past Monday/Tuesday and fills the remaining weekdays too (through Nov 27), ending in a final catch-all 'Suffrigan, Assisting and Retired Bishops' category on Nov 28 (the source's own spelling of 'Suffragan', preserved) -- transcribed as printed, not corrected or reorganized. The diocese-rotation cycle also names PA's own diocese right alongside every other TEC diocese ('Diocese of Pennsylvania', July 28, paired with its own current bishop) -- kept exactly as printed even though it is this same diocese naming itself; this is the source's own genuine content, not an error to omit. Note also: this rotation separately names 'Diocese of Northwestern Pennsylvania' (July 14) and 'Diocese of Susquehanna' (Jan 12) as two of the many OTHER dioceses in its alphabetical companion list -- distinct dioceses from this file's own Diocese of Pennsylvania, transcribed as printed with no special handling; per this task's own instruction not to confuse Pennsylvania with Northwestern Pennsylvania, this note flags that the two names legitimately co-occur here as separate, correctly-distinguished entries.

Wednesday through Saturday of most weeks name one of the diocese's own parishes (a clear 'Congregation Name, Town' pattern, split on the single comma into `parish` type's `name`/`place`), typically paired with a specific rector/priest/deacon (or, for a parish currently without settled clergy, the bare word 'Wardens', or 'Searching'/'Standing Committee: Searching' for a diocese between bishops) in the adjoining column, recorded verbatim in that subject's own `note` field exactly as printed -- including entries that name a lay seminarian-in-charge (Feb 28, 'Kathryn Bross (seminarian in charge)') or a named canon/administrator rather than clergy (Jan 14, 'Canon for Finance' / 'Canon Doug Horner'). Saturdays through much of the file instead name 'Retired Clergy' as a standing `category` subject, with that week's own batch of (typically 4-5) named retired clergy from the adjoining column joined into one `note` field, semicolon-separated, in the order printed; this rotates through the diocese's full retired-clergy roster across many weeks rather than repeating.

A source subject naming what reads as a specific, individually-identifiable congregation (rather than a diocesan office/committee/ministry) is nonetheless recorded as `category`, not `parish`, whenever the source's own text does NOT include a comma-delimited town/city -- this schema's `parish` type requires a `place` field, and none is separately given for these entries, so a town is never guessed or supplied from outside knowledge of the diocese's real parishes. This affects: 'St. Mary's Wayne' (Jan 8) and 'St. Luke's Germantown' (Jan 29) and 'St. Mary's Chester' (Feb 5) (each printed as one run-together phrase with the town but no comma before it); 'George W. South Memorial Church of the Advocate' (Feb 7); 'Grace and the Incarnation' (Jan 24); 'Church of the Holy Apostles and the Mediator' (Apr 9); 'St. Jude and the Nativity' (Apr 17); 'St. Luke and the Epiphany' (May 29); 'Calvary St. Augustine' (Jul 16); 'Philadelphia Cathedral' (Sep 16, the diocese's own cathedral -- 'Philadelphia' happens to appear within its own printed name, but is not set off as a separate place the way this file's ordinary parish entries are); 'African Church of St. Thomas' (Sep 30); 'Church of the Annunciation' (Oct 9); 'Memorial Church of the Good Shepherd' (Oct 21); 'St. Simon the Cyrenian Church' (Nov 6); and 'Christ Church and St. Michael's' (Nov 13). 'Washington Memorial Chapel,' (Sep 10) is the one further edge case: the source prints a trailing comma with nothing after it (evidently an omitted town), transcribed here as `category` with the dangling comma dropped from `name` (the comma itself was clearly a placeholder for missing text, not a content character worth preserving) rather than guessing the town.

Two comma-containing subjects are `category`, not `parish`, because the comma is internal to a province/list name rather than separating a congregation from its town: 'The Anglican Church in Aotearoa, New Zealand and Polynesia' (Dec 14, 2025 -- excluded 2025 content, see above) and 'Suffrigan, Assisting and Retired Bishops' (Nov 28, 2026).

'Christ Church, Old Swedes' (Jul 17) is transcribed as `parish` with place 'Old Swedes' exactly as the source's own comma-delimited text gives it, even though 'Old Swedes' reads as a historic nickname/campus designation rather than an ordinary town -- following the source's own printed structure rather than reinterpreting it. Similarly 'St. Mary's, Cathedral Road' (Sep 24) uses 'Cathedral Road' (a street/area name, not a separate municipality) as printed.

This source is unusually typo-dense; every apparent typo is preserved verbatim, never silently corrected, per this corpus's standing rule. A representative (not exhaustive) sample: 'Canturbury' for Canterbury (Nov 30, 2025, excluded); 'Diosesan' for Diocesan (repeated throughout, e.g. Dec 1, 2025); 'Provice' for Province (Dec 7, 2025, excluded); 'Assiting' for Assisting (Mar 2); '3nd Sunday after Epiphany' for 3rd (Jan 25 liturgical label); 'Communtion' for Communion (Mar 17); 'Vistitation of BVM' for Visitation (Jun 1 liturgical label); 'Pentesost' for Pentecost (May 24 liturgical label); 'Maunday Thursday' for Maundy (Apr 2 liturgical label); 'Jeresulam' for Jerusalem (Feb 4); 'Wisconson' for Wisconsin (Nov 10); 'Dioces of Western New York' for Diocese (Nov 25); 'Stphen' for Stephen (Nov 25); 'Tiwan' for Taiwan (Oct 5); 'Cambell' for Campbell (Oct 11); 'Thre Rev.' and 'The. Rev.' and 'Erv.' as inconsistent renderings of 'The Rev.' (e.g. Apr 18, Feb 15/excluded, Jul 17); 'Falsington' for Fallsington (Jan 3); 'Coatsville' for Coatesville (Aug 27); 'Swathmore' for Swarthmore (Sep 17); 'Grace Ephiphany' for Epiphany (Sep 3); 'Litoral Equador' for Ecuador (Apr 20). None of these are corrected.

Excel cell artifacts (trailing/leading whitespace, stray blank lines within a single cell, e.g. 'Diocese of Alabama' printed with two trailing blank lines in its cell) are trimmed as ordinary spreadsheet formatting, not preserved as content, per this corpus's existing episcopal-northern-michigan-2026.json precedent for the same kind of artifact -- the words themselves are never altered. One source cell (the 3rd Sunday of Advent's Anglican Communion primate line, excluded 2025 content) lists three co-primates of the Anglican Church in Aotearoa, New Zealand and Polynesia on three separate lines within one cell ('The Most Revd Sione Uluiakepa' / 'The Most Revd Justin Duckworth' / 'The Most Revd  Don Tamihere,    Primates'); these are joined into one `note` field with '; ' between them, preserving each line's own internal spacing/punctuation as printed.

One date cell (Wednesday of the 3rd week of Advent, excluded 2025 content) is stored in the source not as a date but as the literal text '12/17/255' (an evident data-entry slip). Its position in the week's own unbroken Mon-Sat sequence (Monday Dec 15 -- Tuesday Dec 16 -- [this cell] -- Thursday Dec 18) leaves no ambiguity that it is Wednesday, December 17, 2025; used as such here since this schema's `date` field requires a valid ISO date and cannot hold the source's garbled text, unlike a `name`/`note` field.

Every parish/category subject's clergy, warden, or other adjoining-column line is recorded in that subject's own `note` field verbatim (joined with '; ' when the source gives more than one name for the same date, e.g. co-rectors or a priest plus a deacon), following this corpus's existing episcopal-delaware-2026.json precedent for a source with no dedicated schema field for this information -- including generic non-personal values printed as-is ('Wardens', 'Searching', 'Standing Committee: Searching').

`diocese` is given as "The Episcopal Diocese of Pennsylvania", the diocese's own name as published on its website (diopa.org) -- the source workbook itself carries no diocese-name title anywhere (only the sheet's own internal title 'Diocesan Intersessions Calendar' and the filename), though one of its own entries (Jul 28) does independently confirm the diocese by naming itself 'Diocese of Pennsylvania' with its own current bishop, The Rt. Rev. Daniel G. P. Gutiérrez.
